content.value_statement: Teams miss security issues when release checks are informal. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured security questions and warning templates.
actual_capabilities: Asks focused questions about user input, data access, secrets, and authorization.
Provides a checklist for input handling, authentication, data exposure, and common vulnerabilities.
Formats results as pass, warning, or critical warning messages.
Includes examples for SQL injection, XSS, IDOR, and hardcoded secrets.
Uses Socratic questions to help teams reason about attack scenarios.
limitations: It is advisory guidance and does not scan code automatically.
It depends on accurate code context from the user or agent.
It does not replace a professional security review for high-risk systems.
It does not run tests, dependency scans, or dynamic application checks.

use_cases.title: Pre-Release Feature Review
use_cases.description: Check a new feature for input validation, authorization, and data exposure risks before launch.

use_cases.title: Security Coaching Session
use_cases.description: Use structured questions to help a developer understand security risks in their implementation.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Risk Triage
use_cases.description: Summarize security concerns from a change and decide which issues need attention before merge.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Security Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the security gate for this feature. Focus on user input, data access, secrets, and obvious release risks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the security gate to this pull request. List pass items, warnings, critical warnings, and questions for the author.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Sensitive Data Handling
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for personal data or secrets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security gate to review how this change handles sensitive data, tokens, logs, errors, and authorization checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Release Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the full security gate and produce a release recommendation. Separate must-fix issues, recommended fixes, residual risks, and owner questions.

output_examples.input: Review a profile update feature before release.
output_examples.output: Security gate warning: user input is accepted, but server-side validation is not documented. Confirm allowed fields, length limits, and ownership checks before release.
Critical warning: the feature exports sensitive data and needs clear admin authorization checks, audit logging, and safe error handling before production use.
Security gate questions: how long do reset tokens last, where are they stored, and what prevents reuse after a successful reset?

best_practices: Provide the relevant code paths, data flows, and user roles before running the gate.
Treat critical warnings as release blockers until a responsible owner accepts the risk.
Document each warning with a location, impact, and follow-up decision.
anti_patterns: Using the gate as a substitute for automated security testing.
Reviewing only happy paths and skipping malicious input cases.
Closing warnings without recording the reason or owner.

faq.question: Does this skill scan my repository automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides a review based on the code and context provided to the agent.

faq.question: Can it find every vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. It covers common review areas and should be paired with tests, scanners, and expert review.

faq.question: What does a critical warning mean?
faq.answer: It means the issue could cause serious harm and should be fixed before production release.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Engineers, reviewers, and leads who need a consistent security check before merge or release.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written as agent guidance and supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Provide changed files, feature goals, expected users, sensitive data, and known security assumptions.
